newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ennex buys option on Kazakstan zinc property.
newsitem.headline: Ennex buys option on Kazakstan zinc property.

text.p: Irish exploration group Ennex International Plc said on Friday that it has signed heads of Agreement to buy an option to purchase a large open-pittable zinc oxide deposit in the former soviet state of Kazakstan. "Work completed to date indicates that it contains in excess of four million tonnes of oxide material at a grade of approximately 24 percent zinc," Ennex said in a statement. If the option is exercised, Ennex can acquire a 95 percent interest in the licence area. This is the first development announced by Ennex since the strengthening of the management team following the recent acquisition of Oranmore Resources Limited, the statement said.

Christian Schaffalitzky, who has been appointed Managing Director of Ennex, said the project requires a relatively small amount of work, due to begin in June, to test as viability. The Shaimarden zinc deposit is situated in northwest Kazakstan using modern hydro-metallurgical technology, it has been estimated that up to one million tonnes of zinc metal could be produced on site. The option period runs to December 31, 1997, the statement said. On signing the agreement, Ennex will pay $125,000 to the Zinc Corporation of Kazakstan which holds a 95 percent unencumbered interest in the Shaimarden licence. Ennex said it will carry out an evaluation programme, including drilling and metallurgical testwork, leading to the commencement of a feasibility study and due diligence. An additional $125,000 will be payable to the Zinc Corporation three months after signing the option. Ennex can at anytime during the option period terminate the agreement without penalty, it said.
